chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dehqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, from Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (the first) (peace be upon him), who said:
Three things clear the vision: looking at greenery, looking at flowing water, and looking at a beautiful face.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that clear the vision according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) links aesthetic pleasure to spiritual clarity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *tazkiyah* (purification) through sensory harmony. The inclusion of the 'beautiful face' (*wajh hasan*) is often interpreted by scholars as referring to the countenance of the Ahl al-Bayt or the divine beauty reflected in creation, bridging the physical and metaphysical realms. This practice underscores the Islamic view that appreciating natural beauty serves as a means to elevate the soul and prepare it for deeper contemplation.
